lines.text: I couldn't find a wine sherwani with matching trousers. Here are some purple options, with cream pants.
The sherwani it needed was right there. In wine. With matching trousers.
The page just said otherwise.
The agent didn't fail. It filtered on exactly what it was told.
Product pages were written for people. People look at the photo, and quietly correct the words.
Agents can't. They filter on text and structured data, and they take it literally.
On this shirt, the title says fawn. The image text says beige. The photo shows grey.
This one is sold as a single shirt, but ships as a jacket and a shirt.
Here, the material says silk. The description says nylon.
Every one of those is a filter that fails without a sound. A missed sale, or a return.
FitCheck reads a product the way an agent does. Every line of text. Every structured field. Every photo.
It checks them against each other, and shows each conflict with both sources, side by side.
Then it rebuilds the data agents filter on. Colour. Pieces. Collar. Length. Embellishment. Sizes in stock. Every value cites where it came from.
Where the page contradicts itself, it doesn't guess. It holds the value back, and asks the brand.
Found one. This sherwani is photographed in deep wine, with a sheer dupatta. The trouser colour isn't confirmed by the brand, so I'd check before ordering.
Same agent. Same question. Now it finds the product, and it's honest about what the page can't prove.
We scanned ten listings from one premium menswear brand.
Eight disagreed with themselves, or with their own photos. Five couldn't agree on how many pieces ship. Eight had structured data a strict parser rejects.
Average readiness went from fifty-seven to seventy-eight, before the brand answered a single question.
Shoppers are starting to hand the search to agents.
Brands can't see what those agents read, or why their products get skipped. Their analytics don't show it. Their search tools weren't built for it.
We're starting with clothing, where colour, fit, and what's in the box decide everything.
Next: any product, and an endpoint any shopping agent can call before it recommends.
Make your catalogue legible to the things that now do the shopping.
FitCheck.
